rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haqq means what is real, established, true, and certain, especially true beliefs, ideas, knowledge, and rulings; batil is its opposite, falsehood.
rows.anchor: hak, “gerçek, sabit ve doğru olan, varlığı kesin olan şey” demek olup

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In religious usage, haqq names divine religion preserved in its original form and schools accepted as representing it most truly; batil includes false belief and religions or schools that lack or lose divine truth.
rows.anchor: Hiçbir bozulmaya uğramadan aslî hüviyetini koruyan ilâhî dine hak din

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haqq also has a legal and ethical sense: material or spiritual resources, shares, goods, and benefits that must be protected, respected, or delivered to their owners.
rows.anchor: korunması, gözetilmesi ya da sahibine ödenmesi gerekli olan maddî veya mânevî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s primary referent is Islam as haqq and polytheism as batil.
rows.anchor: Söz konusu âyetteki hak kelimesinin öncelikli anlamı İslâm dini, bâtılın

rows.speaker: Taberî

rows.anchor: Taberî, âyetteki hak ve bâtıl kelimeleriyle ne kastedildiği hakkında farklı görüşler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author agrees with Tabari: the Qur’an brought haqq, and the Messenger struggled against polytheists to establish haqq and uproot batil in all its senses.
rows.anchor: Kur’an hakkı getirmiştir, Allah’ın elçisi putperestlere karşı bütün anlamlarıyla hakkı

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: müfessirler

rows.anchor: Müfessirler genellikle Kur’an’ın şifa ve rahmet oluşunu mânevî anlamda açıklamışlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an provides guidance for sound religious and worldly life, earns reward for proper recitation, brings forgiveness and divine pleasure, eases hardship, corrects faults, and erases sins.

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zalimun are stubborn deniers of Islam and its truths who replace them with falsehood, especially polytheists and their peers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For these deniers the Qur’an does not heal; their persistence in deviant belief and conduct despite its statements only increases spiritual loss.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’ın beyanlarına rağmen sapkın inanç ve davranışlarında direnmeleri sebebiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human” here means the disbelievers previously called zalimun, not all people.
rows.anchor: “İnsan”dan maksat, bütün insanlar olmayıp önceki âyette “zalimler” diye tanımlanan

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s healing and merciful teaching calls for gratitude in speech and action during blessings, and patience, prayer, and seeking God’s help in hardship.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This response matters religiously and psychologically and morally, as a need of human nature.
rows.anchor: yalnız dinî bakımdan değil, psikolojik ve moral bakımından da önemlidir

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conduct arises from psychological tendencies shaped by innate character and broadly understood education; religious beliefs and moral virtues or failings also shape them.
rows.anchor: insan davranışlarının temeli, onun ruhsal yapısındaki psikolojik eğilimlerdir

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruh means life, breath, or power; as a technical term it is usually understood as the immaterial essence that makes a human what they are, though early theologians sometimes defined it as a subtle body.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some theologians call the soul a subtle body like air; most scholars, especially philosophers, regard it as an independent immaterial reality, individually distinctive and the basis of personal responsibility.
rows.anchor: bazı kelâm âlimleri ruhu hava gibi “latîf bir cisim” kabul ederken başta filozoflar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One argument for the soul is that the body changes and develops while a person’s identity remains stable.
rows.anchor: İnsanın bedeni değişmekte, gelişmekte, başkalaşmaktadır; halbuki onun kişiliği daima aynı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second argument is that moral and legal responsibility would make no sense without a soul, unlike inanimate objects.
rows.anchor: Herkes, insanın ahlâkî, hukukî yönden sorumluluğunu kabul eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third argument is that consciousness, will, and freedom to choose are not bodily properties; the soul exercises them and moves or stops the body.
rows.anchor: İnsandaki bilinç, irade, seçme özgürlüğü gibi yetenek ve kapasitelerin bedene ait

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth argument is that human superiority over physically stronger beings comes from the soul’s reason, mind, judgment, will, and freedom to choose.
rows.anchor: akıl, zihin, muhâkeme, irade, seçme ve karar verme özgürlüğü gibi ruha ait yeteneklerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth argument is that everyone accepts a real human ceases to exist as a person at death because the soul has left the body.
rows.anchor: ölümle birlikte artık cesedin insan olarak varlığının son bulduğunu herkes kabul eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite these arguments, science has not proved the soul’s existence or fully grasped its nature; the verse says humans have been given little knowledge about it.
rows.anchor: ruhun varlığını bilimsel ölçülerle kanıtlamak ve mahiyetini tam olarak kavramak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another broad interpretation takes “you have been given little knowledge” to mean all people possess little knowledge in every field relative to God’s limitless knowledge.
rows.anchor: Bütün insanlara her konuda az bir bilgi verildi

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: The phrase rendered “you will find no protector against Us” can also mean finding no supporter or helper able to restore revelation to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: onu sana geri verebilecek bir destekçi, yardımcı bulamazsın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All knowledge comes from God; He could cause the Prophet and later generations to forget revelation, and no other power could protect, restore, or replace it.
rows.anchor: Dilerse gönderdiği vahyi Peygamber’e ve sonra gelen nesillere unutturmak suretiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier scriptures were largely forgotten or partly altered by people, illustrating their inability to secure divine knowledge by themselves.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’dan önceki kutsal kitapların büyük bir kısmı tamamen, bazısı da kısmen unutulmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could theoretically make Muhammad forget revelation, but mercy means this will not happen in practice; people may still forget it or stray by their own choice and are responsible.
rows.anchor: rahmeti uyarınca bunu fiilen gerçekleştirmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also promises that, through God’s great favor to Muhammad, Islamic revelation will pass from generation to generation without alteration or corruption.
rows.anchor: İslâm vahyinin değişme ve bozulmaya uğramadan nesilden nesile aktarılacağı yönünde bir müjde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses answer those claiming the Qur’an was Muhammad’s own speech: even humans and jinn helping one another cannot produce its equal.
rows.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in Allah tarafından gönderilmediğini, Hz. Muhammed’in sözü olduğunu iddia

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is beyond human production because its expression is beautiful and its content rich and flawless; the commentary links this inimitability to 2:23.
rows.anchor: gerek ifade güzelliği, gerekse içeriğinin zenginliği ve kusursuzluğu dolayısıyla

rows.speaker: İbn İshak
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq’s reported occasion of revelation says prominent Quraysh polytheists gathered by the Kaaba after rejecting the Qur’an’s miraculous superiority and failing to produce its like, then summoned Muhammad.
rows.anchor: İbn İshak’tan nakledilen bir rivayete göre (meselâ bk. Taberî

rows.speaker: Quraysh leaders
rows.claim: The leaders accused Muhammad of dividing their people, insulting ancestors and gods, and harming society; they offered wealth, leadership, or medical help if he acted from greed, ambition, or illness.
rows.anchor: Sen şimdiye kadar Araplar’dan hiç kimsenin yapmadığı kadar halkımız arasında bir ihtilâf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad replied that God sent him with a book and ordered him to warn; accepting his message would benefit them, while rejection left him to wait patiently for God’s judgment.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın kendisini gerçek bir elçi olarak gönderdiğini, kendisine bir kitap indirdiğini

rows.speaker: Quraysh delegation
rows.claim: The delegation then demanded the miracles listed in these verses, alongside removing mountains and reviving an ancestor; Muhammad said performing them was not his mission, repeated his warning, and left saddened.
rows.anchor: konumuz olan âyetlerde belirtilen saçma isteklerini sıraladılar

rows.speaker: Taberî
rows.claim: Hudā, rendered as “guide to salvation,” means revealed knowledge.
rows.anchor: “Kurtuluş rehberi” diye çevirdiğimiz hüdâdan maksat vahiy bilgisidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reason polytheists rejected the Prophet was that he was human rather than angelic; they wrongly assumed messengers must be superhuman and missed why God sends messengers from people’s own kind.
rows.anchor: putperestlerin Hz. Peygamber’e inanmamalarının bir sebebi de, onun melek benzeri bir varlık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If angels lived on earth, God would send an angel messenger to them; an angel sent to humans would be invisible and unable to communicate in their language, defeating the purpose of messengership.
rows.anchor: Eğer yeryüzünde melekler yaşasaydı iletişim kurabilmeleri için Allah onlara elçi olarak melek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 96 reassures the Prophet and warns disbelievers that God knows their stubborn rejection and arrogance despite the clarity and persuasive force of the call.
rows.anchor: davet ve tebliğin bütün açıklığına, ikna ediciliğine rağmen müşriklerin red ve inkârda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists’ hostility grieved the Prophet, who wished them to become Muslims; verse 97 consoles him that God does not guide those who stubbornly deny rather than consider the message rationally and fairly.
rows.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’i teselli maksadı taşıyan 97. âyette risâletin mahiyeti üzerinde akıl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one, including the Prophet, can help or rescue those whom God leaves astray.
rows.anchor: O’nun sapkınlıkla başbaşa bıraktıklarına, peygamber de dahil olmak üzere hiç kimsenin yardım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defiant deniers will be dragged face-first in humiliation at resurrection, made blind, mute, and deaf as punishment for their unjust words and actions against Islam and Muslims, and punished in Hell with unceasing fire.
rows.anchor: mahşerde kör, dilsiz ve sağır bırakılacakları, nihayet varıp kalacakları yerin cehennem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to resurrection denial is that the polytheists contradict themselves: when asked, they acknowledge God created the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: kendilerine sorulduğunda gökleri ve yeri Allah’ın yarattığını söylüyorlardı

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi’s preferred reading of God’s ability to create their likes is that He can create them a second time and resurrect them for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: tercih edilen yoruma göre “ikinci defa yaratmaya, (âhiret hayatı için) yeniden diriltmeye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentaries explain rahma here as wealth and property, so the author translates it as “treasuries of mercy.”
rows.anchor: Tefsirlerde rahmet kelimesi “mal mülk” olarak açıklanmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders’ mocking demands for beneficial miracles in 17:90–93 treated faith as a source of personal gain and revealed material greed; their indifference to the poor shows the same selfishness.
rows.anchor: din konusunu bir menfaat meselesi olarak algıladıklarını ortaya koymuşlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement presents egoism as a deep character trait in people deprived of faith and moral formation.
rows.anchor: iman ve ahlâk terbiyesinden yoksun kalmış her insanda köklü bir ruh hali

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators say the nine signs may mean nine miracles performed through Moses or nine verses/commands of the Torah.
rows.anchor: Müfessirler, buradaki “dokuz âyet”in Hz. Mûsâ’nın elinde gerçekleştirilen dokuz mûcize

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the miracle reading, they are the staff turned serpent, shining hand, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, water from stone, the sea’s parting, and Mount Sinai frightening Israel.
rows.anchor: Yılana dönüşen âsa, ışık saçan el, çekirge, ekin böceği, kurbağa, kan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says two Jews asked Muhammad about the nine signs and he named nine moral and religious commands: avoid polytheism, unlawful killing, adultery, usury, magic, handing over innocents, extravagance, slander, and fleeing battle.
rows.anchor: İki yahudi Hz. Peygamber’e gelerek buradaki “dokuz âyet”le ne kastedildiğini sormuşlar

rows.speaker: Muhammed Hamîdullah
rows.claim: Hamidullah identifies the nine signs as the Ten Commandments in the Torah, excluding the Sabbath prohibition.
rows.anchor: Muhammed Hamîdullah bu dokuz âyetin, Tevrat’taki “on emir”den

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad could not doubt what God revealed about the signs or commands; “ask the Children of Israel” addresses other people who may have doubts.
rows.anchor: Hz. Muhammed’in inanmaması söz konusu olamaz. Bu sebeple âyetteki “İsrâiloğulları’na sor”

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says “you know very well” shows Pharaoh’s denial came from stubbornness, not genuine intellectual inability to be convinced.
rows.anchor: Firavun’un inkârının, gerçekten aklen ikna olmamasından kaynaklanan bir inkâr değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “land” is Egypt, where the Israelites had lived for centuries before crossing to Sinai with Moses.
rows.anchor: yüzyıllardır yaşadıkları Firavunlar ülkesi Mısır’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentaries explain Pharaoh’s attempt to end Israel’s presence in the country as killing or exiling them.
rows.anchor: Firavun’un öldürme, sürgüne tâbi tutma gibi yollarla İsrâiloğulları’nın ülkesindeki varlığına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reversed Pharaoh’s plan by drowning him, his followers, and his army in the water.
rows.anchor: Firavun ve etrafındaki adamları, askerleri suda boğarak bu planı tersine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lands in which Israel was told to settle means Palestine.
rows.anchor: “Topraklar”dan maksat Filistin ülkesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing reminder of afterlife and accountability warns Israelites to fulfill their duties and rejects claims that they are a specially favored people entitled to exceptional treatment.
rows.anchor: İsrâiloğulları’nın bundan sonraki görevlerini hakkıyla yerine getirmeleri uyarısında bulunulmakta
